perspective:
From John Atcitty’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He is John Atcitty, an Alaska Native Heavy Equipment Operator with a middle-school education. He teaches equipment operation at a community center.
- Beverly Yan is his colleague at the community center, an adult-education teacher with a doctorate. They have worked together on projects combining practical and theoretical knowledge.
- During their joint class project, John set up the equipment and told Beverly he hoped it met her expectations. He heard Beverly say she admired how he handled machines and that education is about what you can do with what you know, not just degrees.
- John felt insecure about his education compared to Beverly’s doctorate, then more confident after her praise.
- John thanked Beverly for her kind words and suggested a new workshop combining theory and practice. He heard Beverly say she loved the idea, valued his practical skills, and thought they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, John worried he might not always meet the high standards they had set. He told Beverly this. He heard Beverly appreciate his honesty, suggest realistic goals, and say their combined efforts—not perfection—make projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, John believed Beverly valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner, which increased his sense of worth. He told her he felt able to be open with her. He heard Beverly respect his openness, trust his judgment completely, and want to continue transparency.
- Encouraged, John felt ambitious and proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase their work. He heard Beverly call it a fantastic idea, say it was the perfect way to demonstrate their impact, and agree to start planning.
